rca of the issue: Duplicate dict key in ai_service.GENERATION_TYPES: 'after_interview_thank_you' was declared once at line 116 with the intended new strict schema (exact subject 'Thank You for Meeting With Us', explicit FORBIDDEN words 'unfortunately/we have decided/congratulations/welcome to the board/conditional appointment', 125-200 words, decision-neutral tone), then RE-declared four lines later (line 120) with a much weaker generic schema ({'subject': 'string', 'body': 'string — thanks the applicant...'}). Python dict-literal semantics apply — the SECOND definition wins — so at runtime the strict schema was unreachable and the LLM prompt would use only the loose one, letting 'unfortunately/congratulations/etc.' slip into generated Thank-You emails. Fix (applied by testing agent): removed the duplicate line-120 entry, leaving only the strict schema on line 116. Verified: the after_interview_thank_you generation now consistently returns a decision-neutral body free of the forbidden phrases (see TestAfterInterviewThankYou::test_decision_neutral). No other Batch 3 code changes needed.
